author: Emily Malia
title: Girl, 14, has arm and leg bitten off in shark attack at Florida beach - and survives - NewsBreak
text:
By Emily Malia ,
35 minutes ago Lulu Gribbin was just an ordinary teenager enjoying a beach day with friends when she was savagely attacked by a shark.
The young girl was on a delightful mother-daughter trip to Seacrest Beach in Florida with her pals when the unthinkable occurred.
Their vacation to the Gulf Coast involved swimming and diving for sand dollars, but it turned into a scene straight out of a horror movie when a shark suddenly attacked.
Lulu remembers the moment they were swimming and her friend yelled, "Shark!" She describes how they all instinctively swam for their lives, not fully processing the situation.
Despite the panic, Lulu remembered advice she'd been given and tried to stay calm, as she'd learned that sharks are often attracted to frantic movement in the water.
She shared with People Magazine the exact moment she realized that might not have been the best course of action.
"So I calmed down, and then I lifted my arm out of the water, and I could see like the flesh on my arm. And that's when I realized... this was a very real situation," she recounted.
The rest is a haze, as she lost consciousness in the water. Her only memory from those terrifying moments is waking up on the Florida beach, surrounded by people attempting to save her life.
Anna Blair, Lulu's devastated mother, had popped out for lunch with the other parents, and as they were heading back, that's when they sensed something was terribly wrong. The girls weren't picking up their phones, and in a panic, they rushed down to the shoreline.
Upon reaching the scene, Blair's other daughter informed her, "Mum, it's Lulu."
She said: "I just remember screaming, like I didn't know what else to do. Ellie kind of calmed me down. It was like a scene out of a movie."
Two teenage girls sustained injuries from the shark and were taken to different hospitals.
South Walton Fire District Chief Ryan Crawford released a statement explaining one victim had "significant injuries to one upper and one lower extremity, both requiring the application of tourniquets," and the other victim received "flesh wounds" to her right foot.
However, they weren't the only casualties. Just an hour prior to the teenager's attack, a 45-year-old woman was also in the water nearby and suffered severe bites to her abdomen, pelvis and left arm.
Lulu's mother described the moment she discovered her daughter on the sand, saying: "I didn't know that her hand was bitten off because they had covered it up.
"And then I could see her leg, and like, that was probably the worst part because her leg was gone basically. And it's something that, like, I can see it right now. I will never unsee it."
The ride to the hospital was torturous for LuLu's mother, who spent the entire journey praying that her daughter was still alive.
Upon arrival, doctors quickly decided to amputate Lulu's leg. They knew that even if they attempted to save it, future amputation would be inevitable.
Following this, the 14-year-old was taken to Ortho Carolina's Reconstructive Center for Lost Limbs in North Carolina, where she endured a lengthy recovery period of 77 days.
As a teenager, Lulu had to essentially restart her life, mastering basic tasks with just one arm and one leg.
In rehab, she learned how to dress herself, brush her teeth, use the restroom, and perform all these routine daily activities that she previously took for granted.
"There were so many other patients that were in worse conditions than me and that didn't even have the option to do half the stuff that I was doing," she expressed.
"They would give anything to be in my position. So I was just grateful that I had the opportunity to do what they were teaching."
Despite the immense trauma she experienced, her positive outlook remained unshaken, and it was this resilience that propelled her towards a successful recovery and a new life with prosthetics.
Mastering her prosthetics was somewhat of a "mental block" for Lulu, who was now adjusting to moving with metal. However, she managed to receive prosthetics sooner than anticipated, and certainly earlier than most individuals in her situation.
"My situation is an anomaly. Most people get prosthetics a very long time after they are amputated," Lulu revealed. Her mother chimed in: "She walked out of the hospital, which is extremely unheard of."
The teenager has since revisited that exact beach, where a shark attack forever altered her life.
She recalled: "I just laid in the sand like how I was laying in the sand when all the paramedics were over me. That was very emotional."
